[RFCS.6.8] **The `event_id` derivation.** An engine must derive each
`FactAssert`'s `event_id` ([LFST.5.6]) by this function, and no other. Let $r$
and $t$ be the UTF-8 bytes of the run identifier and the tier identifier the
integrator gave the engine, each empty when absent ([NLFC.1.2]); $s$ the
`FactAssert`'s `seq` ([LFST.5.3]); $\operatorname{be}_{64}(s)$ its eight bytes,
most significant first; $\Vert$ concatenation; and $\texttt{1F}$ the single
byte 0x1F. The literal is the bytes of its ASCII characters.

$$h = \operatorname{SHA\text{-}256}\bigl(\texttt{"ds.rfcs.event\_id.v1"} \Vert \texttt{1F} \Vert r \Vert \texttt{1F} \Vert t \Vert \texttt{1F} \Vert \operatorname{be}_{64}(s)\bigr)$$

$$u_i = h_i \;\; (0 \le i < 16,\ i \ne 6, 8), \qquad u_6 = (h_6 \wedge \texttt{0F}) \vee \texttt{80}, \qquad u_8 = (h_8 \wedge \texttt{3F}) \vee \texttt{80}$$

$h_i$ is byte $i$ of the digest, counting from 0, and $\wedge$ and $\vee$ are
bitwise. The two assignments set the UUID version to 8 and the variant to the
standard one.

The `event_id` is $u_0 \ldots u_{15}$ written as 32 lower-case hexadecimal
digits, two per byte with the high nibble first, in groups of 8, 4, 4, 4 and 12
digits separated by `-`: 36 characters.
